c02.proof:
by
  intro G H J g h j f q hf hq P hP
  let F : Theory.Hom g j :=
    { toFun := fun x => q (f x)
      map_mul := fun x y => (congrArg q (hf x y)).trans (hq (f x) (f y)) }
  refine ⟨F, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x
    rfl
  · exact Theory.preimage_mul_closed F P hP
c02.bridge: Construct the composite Hom locally; equality transport followed by the second preservation equation proves its map_mul field. Transport the supplied target closure.

c03.proof:
by
  intro G H J g h j f q hf hq P Q hP hQ
  let F : Theory.Hom g (Foundation.prodGroup h j) :=
    { toFun := fun x => (f x, q x)
      map_mul := fun x y => Prod.ext (hf x y) (hq x y) }
  have closed : Theory.MulClosed (Foundation.prodGroup h j)
      (fun z => P z.1 ∧ Q z.2) := by
    intro u v hu hv
    exact ⟨hP u.1 v.1 hu.1 hv.1, hQ u.2 v.2 hu.2 hv.2⟩
  refine ⟨F, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x
    rfl
  · exact Theory.preimage_mul_closed F (fun z => P z.1 ∧ Q z.2) closed
c03.bridge: Construct a paired Hom and coordinatewise preservation locally. Prove closure of the simultaneous target predicate from the two supplied closures, then transport it.

c04.proof:
by
  intro G H g h f q hf hq
  let F : Theory.Hom g (Foundation.prodGroup h h) :=
    { toFun := fun x => (f x, q x)
      map_mul := fun x y => Prod.ext (hf x y) (hq x y) }
  have diagonal : Theory.MulClosed (Foundation.prodGroup h h)
      (fun z => z.1 = z.2) := by
    intro u v hu hv
    change h.mul u.1 v.1 = h.mul u.2 v.2
    exact (congrArg (fun z => h.mul z v.1) hu).trans
      (congrArg (h.mul u.2) hv)
  refine ⟨F, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro x
    rfl
  · exact Theory.preimage_mul_closed F (fun z => z.1 = z.2) diagonal
c04.bridge: Construct the paired Hom locally and show the diagonal predicate closed using coordinate equality transport. Its preimage is the equalizer constraint; no commutativity is assumed.

c05.bridge: Bool XOR has a closed neutral singleton. Complement maps true to that singleton, while true XOR true maps outside; complement does not preserve XOR. Finite witnesses refute the omitted premise.

c06.bridge: The identity map preserves Bool XOR. The singleton true is not multiplication closed because true XOR true is false. This isolates the missing target-closure premise.
